question.problem:
The following table shows the water drainage rate of a reservoir over a period of $8$ hours, starting at $2\,\text{p.m}.$

| $t\,(\text{hours})$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R(t)\,(\text{gallons/hour})$ | $2$ | $k$ | $5$ | $4$ | $3$ |

If the right Riemann sum approximation of the total water drained from $2\,\text{p.m}$ to $10\,\text{p.m.}$ has a value of $30$ gallons, then what is the value of $k?$ 

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the curve (rate vs. time) can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{R(4)+R(6)+R(8)+R(10)}})\cdot {{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of the rate at each point:

| $t$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R(t)$ | $k$ | $5$ | $4$ | $3$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(k+5+4+3)\cdot 2 \\  & =2(k+12) \\  & =2k+24\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total water drained from $2\,\text{p.m}$ to $10\,\text{p.m}.$ Since we are given that the right Riemann sum approximation of the total drainage is $30$ gallons, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2k+24 & =30 \\ 2k & =30-24 \\ k & =\frac{6}{2} \\ k & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
